The bulk of Angrist's research has concentrated on the economics of education, beginning with the returns to schooling. In one early study, Angrist and Krueger exploited the relationship between children's season of birth and educational attainment that is due to policies and laws setting ages for school start and compulsory schooling, finding that returns to education are close to their [OLS estimates](/wiki/Ordinary_least_squares "Ordinary least squares")[[20]](#cite_note-20) and that compulsory attendance laws constrain roughly 10% of students to stay in school who would have otherwise left.[[21]](#cite_note-21) Another early attempt at using IV to estimate returns to schooling by Angrist and Krueger was to exploit the [Vietnam-era draft lottery](/wiki/Draft_lottery_(1969) "Draft lottery (1969)").[[22]](#cite_note-22) However, while their later research on split-sample IVs confirmed the findings of their compulsory schooling research, it failed to support the returns to schooling estimates derived from the draft-lottery research.[[23]](#cite_note-23) Angrist further used variation in U.S. compulsory schooling laws in research with [Daron Acemoglu](/wiki/Daron_Acemoglu "Daron Acemoglu") in order to estimate human-capital [externalities](/wiki/Externalities "Externalities"), which they found to be about 1% and not statistically significant.[[24]](#cite_note-24) Angrist has also studied the strong decrease in the economic returns to schooling in the [West Bank](/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank") and [Gaza Strip](/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip") in the 1980s.[[25]](#cite_note-25) Together with Lavy, Angrist has also explored the returns to schooling in [Morocco](/wiki/Morocco "Morocco"), exploiting a change in its language of instruction from French to Arabic to find that policy substantially reduced Moroccan youths' returns to schooling by deteriorating their French writing skills.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

As of April 2026, Cocomelon is the [3rd most-subscribed](/wiki/List_of_most-subscribed_YouTube_channels "List of most-subscribed YouTube channels") and [2nd most-viewed](/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_channels "List of most-viewed YouTube channels") channel on YouTube,[[1]](#cite_note-1) with over 200 million subscribers and over 220.04 billion views.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

The channel launched in September 2006 and was rebranded as Cocomelon in 2018. It has since expanded globally in multiple languages, with spinoff series, [Netflix](/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") TV shows, [merchandising](/wiki/Merchandising "Merchandising"), special events, and ongoing product diversification. It was purchased by Candle Media in 2021 for a reported $3 billion.
